turns.t: Hello! I've come about a rash, and I've got to say, it's the strangest thing, because I've been on a course of tablets from the dentist, for a tooth, and I started to itch on day four.
Let's slow down. When did the rash appear?
Day five, so yesterday morning. It started on my chest, and now it's on my back and my arms. Little red blotches.
Do they itch?
Terribly. I was scratching in the night, my husband said I was like a dog with fleas.
Any swelling of your lips, tongue or face? ~
No, nothing like that, thank goodness. ~
Any trouble breathing, or feeling faint? ~
Not at all. ~
Have you got a fever? ~
No, I've felt fine. Apart from the itching and the tooth. ~
Are you still taking the tablets? ~
I took the last one yesterday, I had a five-day course. ~
Right, so it's finished. Let me look at your skin. Roll up your sleeves. ~
Of course. I'm a hairdresser, so my arms are usually fine, but I've had to wear long sleeves.
I'll check the blotches.
Is it nasty? ~
Pink, flat blotches over the chest, back and arms, and no blistering. Nothing worrying. ~
Is it the tablets, do you think? ~
It's likely linked, since the timing fits, so the dentist will want to choose something different next time. ~
Oh good, I'd hate to have it again. ~
It should fade by itself over a few days. A cool shower, and loose cotton clothing, will help the itch.
And my tooth? ~
Go back to the dentist and tell them about the rash. They'll choose a different treatment if you still need one.
Right. I do still have a bit of a toothache. ~
Then do ring them today, and mention the rash. Please. ~
I will. Do you think it'll get worse? ~
It usually peaks and settles, but if you develop swelling of the face or lips, difficulty breathing, blistering, or a fever, call 999 or come straight in.
Understood. Thanks ever so much. ~
You're welcome. Take care. ~

clinical_actions.description: Cool showers and loose cotton clothing for the itch
Tell the dentist about the rash and ask for a different treatment
Safety-net: 999 or come in for facial swelling, breathing difficulty, blistering or fever
